parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State what is meant by the work function energy of a metal.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem: Ultraviolet radiation of frequency $1.36 \times 10^{15} \text{Hz}$ is incident, in a vacuum, on a metal surface. The power of the radiation incident on the surface is $8.36 \text{mW}$. Photoelectrons are emitted with a maximum kinetic energy of $3.09 \times 10^{-19} \text{J}$.
parts.text: Determine the number of photons incident on the surface per unit time.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate the work function energy $\Phi$ of the metal.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem:
The frequency of the radiation incident on the surface in (b) is increased while the power remains constant.

State and explain the effect of this change on:
parts.text: the maximum kinetic energy of the photoelectrons

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: the rate of emission of photoelectrons.
